## Purpose and scope

This protocol takes the curated OTU table and the taxonomic identifications produced by EnGeL-BIOINF-OBITOOLS4 and prepares them for community analysis: it keeps the OTUs that received an identification, converts read counts into presence/absence (incidence) data, and shows which OTUs are shared between groups of samples (for example treatments, sites or methods) with a Venn diagram. The incidence table is also the input for sampling-effort and completeness analyses (EnGeL-SAMPL-EFFORT).

## Principle

The OTU table (OTUs × samples, read counts) is joined to the identification table by OTU name, so that only OTUs with an identification are kept. Because read numbers in metabarcoding do not translate directly into abundance, each count is turned into presence (1) or absence (0). An OTU is counted as present in a group when it occurs in at least one sample of that group; the overlaps between groups are drawn as a Venn diagram (Gao et al., 2021).

## Reagent preparation

**Sample-group table.** Create `data/raw/sample_groups.csv` with one row per sample column of the OTU table: column `sample` (exactly as in the OTU table) and column `group`. Negative controls (extraction blanks, PCR negatives) get their own group, for example `blank`.

```
sample,group
PA1,BF3_BR2_Novogene
PA2,BF3_BR2_Novogene
PCB,blank
```

## Procedure

### 1. Set up

(@) Open the project's R project (paths below are relative to the project folder; do not use `setwd()` with personal paths).
(@) Load the packages:

```r
library(readxl)
library(tibble)
library(writexl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggVennDiagram)
```

### 2. Read and join the tables

(@) Read the identification table and the curated OTU table, and check the dimensions (OTUs × samples) against the EnGeL-BIOINF-OBITOOLS4 report:

```r
tax <- as.data.frame(read_xlsx("data/raw/curated_OTUs_identification_result_MatchesOnly.xlsx"))
otu <- as.data.frame(read.delim("data/raw/otutable_curated.tsv"))
dim(otu)
```

(@) Give both tables the same OTU column name and keep only OTUs that have an identification:

```r
colnames(tax)[colnames(tax) == "id"] <- "otu"
otu <- rownames_to_column(otu, var = "otu")
otu_kept <- merge(otu, tax, by = "otu")
dim(otu_kept)
write_xlsx(otu_kept, "results/otutable_keptOTUs.xlsx")
```

(@) Keep only the sample columns, with OTU names as row names:

```r
groups  <- read.csv("data/raw/sample_groups.csv")
samples <- intersect(groups$sample, colnames(otu_kept))
counts  <- otu_kept[, samples]
rownames(counts) <- otu_kept$otu
```

::: {.callout-important title="CRITICAL"}
Every sample column of the OTU table must appear in the sample-group table, spelled the same way. Check that `length(samples)` equals the number of samples you expect.
:::

### 3. Incidence (presence/absence)

(@) Convert read counts to presence/absence (1/0) and save the incidence table:

```r
incidence <- counts %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ ifelse(. > 0, 1, 0)))
write_xlsx(rownames_to_column(incidence, "otu"), "results/OTU_incidence.xlsx")
```

### 4. OTUs shared between groups

(@) List, for each group, the OTUs present in at least one of its samples (leave out the negative controls unless you want to show them):

```r
use   <- setdiff(unique(groups$group), "blank")
venn  <- lapply(use, function(g) {
  cols <- groups$sample[groups$group == g]
  rownames(incidence)[rowSums(incidence[, cols, drop = FALSE]) > 0]
})
names(venn) <- use
```

(@) Draw and save the Venn diagram (8 × 6 inches, 300 dpi):

```r
venn_plot <- ggVennDiagram(venn) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#EDD9A3", high = "#F8765C") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = .2))
ggsave("results/venn_plot.png", plot = venn_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

The diagram works for two to four groups; with more groups, use a table of shared OTUs instead [TO CONFIRM: preferred alternative, e.g. an UpSet plot].

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Fewer samples than expected after selecting columns | Sample names differ between the OTU table and the sample-group table | Compare `colnames(otu_kept)` with `groups$sample`; correct the table. |
| Almost no OTUs kept after the join | OTU names differ between the two tables (e.g. a prefix), or the identification column is not called `id` | Compare the first OTU names in both tables and rename as needed. |
| Venn diagram unreadable | Too many groups | Use at most four groups, or a table of shared OTUs. |

## Remarks

The source analysis compared three primer and library-preparation combinations for COI metabarcoding of mesofauna (BF3/BR2 and III_BF3/Fol-degen-rev, prepared by two providers), with one sample group per combination and a blank; the groups and file names above follow it as an example. In the source, the blank was included in one of the groups when drawing the Venn diagram [TO CONFIRM: intended?].
